Summary  
Data source overview: The paper proposes a decentralised on-line “AI marketplace” as a new diffusion mechanism for AI models and data. It analyses the core technical, economic and regulatory problems that currently prevent wide, safe and equitable AI adoption and sketches concrete architectural and governance solutions (privacy-preserving training, open standards, blockchain audit trails, fair pricing, quality verification, etc.).

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83] – Reasonably high confidence that all main causal-interventional chains in the article are captured and connected. Remaining uncertainty is chiefly in edge-type granularity and maturity assessments because the paper is conceptual, not empirical.

Inference strategy justification: Where the authors give only high-level guidance (e.g., “marketplace should facilitate differential privacy”), I infer the corresponding concrete intervention (“Apply differential privacy to all data transferred”) and mark the maturity as low (2) with confidence 2.

Extraction completeness explanation: Every top-level risk named in Section 3 (interoperability, data cooperation, privacy, malicious contributors, information asymmetry, and high cost) is represented. All proposed remedies appearing in Sections 4–6 are decomposed into white-box component interventions and linked through intermediate concept nodes, yielding a single connected fabric.

Key limitations:  
1. Article length required node compression; some minor economic sub-issues had to be folded into umbrella concepts.  
2. Evidence strength is mostly “medium” or “weak” because the paper is a position piece, not an empirical study.  
3. Exact lifecycle phase assignment can vary depending on an organisation’s development workflow.
